HD현대로보틱스 제공 HD현대로보틱스가 국내 최초로 자체 개발한 1t급 초대형 로봇(사진)을 산업 현장에 공급하며 고중량 작업 자동화 시장 공략에 속도를 낸다. HD현대의 로봇 솔루션 전문기업 HD현대로보틱스는 18일 경기 안산 한국R&D 본사에서 1t급 초대형 로봇 ‘HDT1000-33’의 첫 판매 기념행사를 열었다고 밝혔다. 이날 행사에는 김완수 HD현대로보틱스 대표와 허남석 안산시 부시장, 박범열 한국R&D 대표, 문재영 HD건설기계 대표 등이 참석했다. 이번에 공급된 ‘HDT1000-33’은 최대 1t의 가반하중을 갖춘 6축 다관절 로봇이다. 가반하중은 로봇이 들어 올리거나 운반할 수 있는 최대 중량을 뜻한다. 에너지 효율을 높인 설계로 대형·고중량 부품을 다루는 제조 현장 자동화에 최적화된 모델로 평가받는다. 초도 물량은 건설기계용 대형 엔진 생산 공정에 투입된다. 무거운 실린더 엔진 블록을 가공 설비에 넣고, 가공이 끝난 제품을 다음 공정으로 옮기는 작업을 맡을 예정이다. 대형 부품을 단순히 옮기는 데 그치지 않고 설비 투입과 공정 간 이동 같은 복합 작업까지 수행할 수 있다. 정밀도와 안전성도 강점이다. 정밀한 동작 제어 기술을 적용해 수천 번 움직여도 목표 위치와의 오차가 0.1㎜ 이내에 불과하다. 대형 부품을 들어 올려 옮기고 설비에 넣는 작업을 로봇이 대신하면서 작업자가 중량물을 직접 다룰 일도 줄어든다. 중대재해 위험요인을 낮출 수 있다는 게 회사 측 설명이다. 최근 제조 현장에선 대형 모듈화 생산이 확대되면서 한 번에 더 크고 무거운 부품을 다루는 사례가 늘고 있다. 이에 따라 높은 가반하중과 정밀도를 함께 갖춘 초대형 로봇 수요가 증가하는 추세다. HD현대로보틱스는 이 같은 흐름에 맞춰 2024년 2월 1t급 초대형 로봇 개발에 착수했고, 2년 9개월 만에 첫 판매 성과를 냈다. HD현대로보틱스는 초대형 로봇의 적용 범위를 조선 기자재, 차량용 대형 부품, 전기차 배터리팩 등 고중량 부품을 다루는 산업으로 넓혀 신규 시장을 발굴할 방침이다. 김 대표는 “그간 자동화가 어려웠던 고중량 작업도 자동화가 가능해져 제조 현장의 중대재해 위험요인이 대폭 줄어들 것”이라며 “초대형 로봇과 피지컬 인공지능(AI)을 미래 양대 성장축으로 삼아 시장을 선도하겠다”고 말했다. 송준영 기자 ssong@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 송준영 산업부에서 주로 중공업 분야를 취재하고 있습니다. 조선과 방산, 정유·석유화학, 철강, 항공·해운 업계를 출입하며 에너지와 전력기기, 배터리·첨단소재 등 제조업 현장의 소식을 전합니다. items.fullText: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities November 15, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents. At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world. Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage. “It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.” Community leaders share how they build with open models and tools at AI Day Seoul. The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum November 9, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT -NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX. Representatives from the Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA met with over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI semiconductors. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2 , with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies , RLWRLD and Upstage. Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure. Motif Technologies , a Seoul-based AI lab, develops foundation models for building AI agents that carry out complex tasks, including Motif-3, a large language model released with open weights. RLWRLD, a physical AI startup based in San Francisco, Seoul and Tokyo, develops robotics foundation models that enable humanoid and industrial robots to perform complex real-world tasks that require five-finger dexterity, such as precisely inserting components, threading nuts onto bolts and kitting parts from moving conveyors. Upstage , a Korean enterprise AI company, develops Solar language models and document AI tools that help businesses extract information from complex documents, streamline workflows and build AI applications for everyday operations. The companies represent work across the full AI stack , from infrastructure to models to robotics applications. items.fullText: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA November 8, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Tapping into the country’s strengths in manufacturing and engineering, NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem. The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles. These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production. Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering. In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST . Samsung is also exploring NVIDIA cuEquivariance to speed up tensor operations used in training and inference for atomistic AI models. Samsung is developing chip-scale thermal and mechanical analysis workflows with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo . In one AI homogenization case, combining AI-predicted effective material properties, coarser grids and GPU acceleration resulted in a roughly 1,600x speedup. Simulation time fell from about 18 hours for a fine-grid solve on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds for a GPU-accelerated coarse-grid solve. Looking ahead, NVIDIA Agent Toolkit could connect these simulation tools and AI models, helping future engineering agents run analyses and compare design options.
